Client-provided dataset contains 100,000 records and 100 columns after a validated one-to-one merge. Churn is defined as occurrence between 31 and 60 days after observation date in the provided overview.

ROC-AUC measures ranking quality, not the probability that an offer will save a customer.

LightGBM native categorical binary classifier. 75/25 stratified split; validation rows=25,000; seed 42; early stopping selected 734 iterations. AUC is 0.7021, average precision 0.6871. Internal validation is a random holdout, not a future-time test.

Calculation: top-20 validation cohort mean monthly rev_Mean=54.57697 dataset units. Revenue preserved per targeted customer = 54.57697 × 12 × assumed incremental retention uplift. Net revenue proxy subtracts assumed offer cost of 10 dataset units. Break-even uplift=10/(54.57697×12)=1.5269 pp. Costs and uplift are hypothetical; contribution margin, discount cannibalization, currency, and causal treatment effect are not known.

title: Offer help that matches the observed problem

text: Offer help that matches the observed problem
External evidence supports testing targeted retention; it does not transfer an uplift estimate to Company A.
Risk score identifies who to review
Service review identifies what to fix

• Older handset → check device condition

• Falling usage → ask about coverage, plan fit, or service friction

• High value + high risk → prioritize human follow-up

• Diagnose first; offer a plan change or device support only when it fits

• Keep a no-offer control group

• Record contact, offer, acceptance, cost, and 60-day outcome
Capponi et al. (2021) report positive retention effects from anti-churn campaigns in one Italian mobile-operator sample; Company A must establish its own effect experimentally.

Capponi, Corrocher & Zirulia (2021), Telecommunications Policy 45(1), 102069, DOI 10.1016/j.telpol.2020.102069: find positive retention effects in one Italian operator sample. The result motivates a test; it is not a Company A effect estimate.

Recommendation: randomize high-risk eligible customers to treatment or control, stratifying by risk band and equipment-age/usage group. Power analysis is required before launch. Primary outcome is churn in the assignment’s 31–60 day window; include later revenue and contribution after costs, not only AUC.

title: Limits that must shape the decision

text: Limits that must shape the decision
Source: supplied dataset and validation; these are material constraints.
Prediction is not treatment effect
AUC 0.702 ranks risk; it does not show which customer an offer will save.
Historical sample
Random holdout is not a future-time test; validate on a later period before production.
Incomplete business context
The materials do not document currency, operator market, intervention costs, or contribution margins.
Proxy and data-quality risk
Area and household descriptors rank highly; audit fairness, missingness, and category stability.

The proposal intentionally treats unit economics as a scenario only. The client brief anonymizes Company A and does not state the currency or market. The validation split is random rather than chronological. Area and household variables may be proxies and need governance review before any operational targeting.

title: A 90-day path from analysis to evidence

text: A 90-day path from analysis to evidence
Recommended next step: approve a limited randomized pilot, not a full deployment.
Days 1–30
Validate data & costs
Confirm currency, margins, offer cost, eligibility, and future-period validation.
Days 31–60
Run the randomized pilot
Contact treated high-risk customers; keep a control; log actions and outcomes.
Days 61–90
Read out and decide
Compare churn and contribution; report uncertainty; scale only if net value is positive.
Decision gate: positive incremental contribution versus control, with no material deterioration in complaints or fairness checks.

Plan assumes stakeholders can provide economics and approve random assignment. A statistically powered test sample and confidence interval should be set before launch. If the pilot effect is weak or negative, revise the intervention or targeting rather than expanding spend.
